_comment: TCO parameter defaults for eflips-impact. Every block below is written into a
'tco_parameters' JSONB column and must match the shape eflips.impact.tco expects
(see eflips.impact.tco.dataclasses).
There is one block per kind of row, and no per-vehicle-type overrides. The
upstream eflips-impact files key everything by 'name_short', which only works for
a fixed fleet of known models; django-simba fleets come from user uploads with
arbitrary names, so such a list matched nothing and every row fell through to the
default anyway. Diesel keeps a block of its own because it is priced differently,
and the costs page is where a fleet that needs per-type numbers sets them.
'scenario' mirrors the db_default of Scenario.tco_parameters plus 'eta_avail',
which eflips.impact.tco.TCOCalculator reads unconditionally.
'lifetimes' is the only place a vehicle, battery or charging point lifetime is
written, for either calculation. The blocks below therefore carry no
'useful_life' of their own: ebustoolbox.impact._apply_lifetimes stamps it onto
every row after they are seeded, and ensure_lca_parameters feeds the same three
numbers to the LCA. They used to be duplicated here and in lca_overrides.json /
lca.json, and had drifted apart -- a bus was written off over 14 years by the TCO
and 12 by the LCA, a battery over 7 and 8. eflips-impact noticed the second one
and warned about it on every single LCA run.
'charging_infrastructure' is the exception and keeps its useful_life: it is the
cost of the site itself, has no LCA counterpart to agree with, and is not
editable on the costs page.
